articles.title: Give Me the Ball! review – tennis trailblazer Billie Jean King is ferocious force for equality
articles.summary: Sparky and engaging documentary about the ‘battle of the sexes’ player, who fought her whole career to ensure the women’s game got the respect it deserved. After the engaging Evert and Navratilova documentary Chris and Martina: The Final Set comes this watchable and engaging documentary portrait of…
body: King (née Moffitt) was a ferocious force in women’s tennis from the 60s onwards and a vehement but polite advocate for equal rights on prize money. The women’s game was equally skilful, though not possessed of the same brutal brawn-power, and sold as many stadium seats. King sensationally helped to launch the Virginia Slims women’s tour – one of the great commercial revolutions in US sports, and had to work hard on promotion and sponsorship at the same time as simply training and playing. And while all this was happening, she had to come to terms with her gay sexuality, while married to the poignantly devoted Larry King, who is a gallantly supportive interviewee here.

In the 80s, King was put through another ordeal when her vengeful ex-partner Marilyn Barnett sued for “galimony”, thus revealing King’s sexuality to the world, which again she had to face out at a press conference in the company of her husband and bewildered parents. This is an enjoyable film, though I was surprised that no male tennis player could be found to praise King’s importance, not even the otherwise ubiquitous John McEnroe.
points: Sparky and engaging documentary about the ‘battle of the sexes’ player, who fought her whole career to ensure the women’s game got the respect it deserved.

articles.title: Female Perversions review – Tilda Swinton searches for erotic adventures in rework of Madame Bovary
articles.summary: The actor’s 1996 first US film, as a lawyer trying to manage her complicated love life and traumatic fantasies, marked her out as a screen presence like no other. Tilda Swinton made her US debut 30 years ago with this insouciant, startling, experimental adventure in eroticism and neuroticism.
body: Streitfeld’s fictional reworking does not focus on Emma Bovary. Instead Swinton plays a character called Eve, a brilliant, beautiful – and single – lawyer with an elegant, angular style; she is as graceful and sometimes comically clumsy as a baby giraffe. Eve is having a passionate affair with a hunky seismologist called John (Clancy Brown), an amusing metaphor for the quake-level sex they’re having. She is also deeply attractive and attracted to women, yet also assailed by traumatised fantasies or flashbacks of something in her past; there are terrible lurches of guilt or fear, abuse, loss, self-harm or impostor syndrome.
points: The actor’s 1996 first US film, as a lawyer trying to manage her complicated love life and traumatic fantasies, marked her out as a screen presence like no other.

articles.title: NAZA documentary on Gaza killings becomes one of year’s most watched
articles.summary: The film, which details Israel’s surveillance of Palestinian civilians, has been seen by more than 1.5m people in less than two months. NAZA, the award-winning documentary that details Israel’s mass killing of civilians in Gaza, has been seen by more than 1.5 million people since being released in…
body: The film, which is directed by the Oscar-winning Israeli film-makers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor and produced by the Guardian, has reached a worldwide audience of 1,547,033 as of Friday 6 November, making it one of the most-watched documentary films with a theatrical release in 2026.

NAZA won the Special Jury prize at the Venice film festival in September, where its premiere was met with a record 24.5 minute standing ovation, and has received widespread critical acclaim. It drew worldwide attention after Israel’s culture minister threatened to strip its directors of their citizenship and prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the identification and prosecution of the film’s interviewees.

After a cinematic run in 47 territories to date, the investigative documentary’s free global streaming release on theguardian.com is now planned for early December, as the Guardian works to prepare the online video release for a large global audience in multiple languages.
points: The film, which details Israel’s surveillance of Palestinian civilians, has been seen by more than 1.5m people in less than two months.

articles.title: ‘Adolescence’ Writer Jack Thorne Adapts Matt Haig’s ‘The Humans’ for London’s West End With ‘House of the Dragon’ Star Matt Smith
articles.summary: Matt Smith will play an alien inside the body of a Cambridge academic in “The Humans,” a stage adaptation of Matt Haig’s novel by “Adolescence” writer Jack Thorne. The play will have its world premiere in London’s West End next year.
body: Smith’s character is never named. He is an extraterrestrial sent to Earth to stop humanity’s progress, which is seen as a threat. He takes over the body of Andrew Martin, a mathematics professor at Cambridge. Living as Martin, he sees humanity at its worst and its best, and he is changed by it.
Melting Pot and Second Half Productions are producing in association with Access Entertainment, Len Blavatnik and Danny Cohen’s company, which owns the Haymarket.

“I love ‘The Humans,’ the chance to work on Matt Haig’s beautiful book with Jeremy Herrin has been an absolute dream. It is a story, at its heart, about an alien learning the complexity of beauty, and I can’t think of a more beautiful alien than Matt Smith,” Thorne said.

Haig said that “The Humans” may be the most personal of his novels, which makes him protective of it. “I am a massive fan of Jack Thorne and as soon as I saw his incredible script I knew this was being elevated into something very special indeed. And Matt Smith is the absolutely perfect protagonist for this story. He was almost designed for this role. It looks like people will be surprised in all the right ways,” he said.

The play will have its world premiere in London’s West End next year.

articles.title: Taiwan Creative Content Fest Takeaways: ‘Avatar’ VFX House Brings Its AI Ambitions to Taipei as Character IP Booms
articles.summary: Taiwan Creative Content Fest (TCCF) wrapped its 2026 edition in Taipei with a reshaped show floor, as animation and character IP companies moved to the front of the market.
body: Elsewhere on the floor, television and media networks rose from 20 to 22 exhibitors, and new media, streaming and entertainment companies from six to eight. Film and TV production and distribution companies dropped from 22 to 16, digital tech, VFX and immersive media from 15 to eight, and publishing, comics and webtoons from 12 to five.

The Pitching program presented 93 projects and stories, including entries from TAICCA School, to industry participants from 28 countries. TAICCA is still compiling buyer attendance and the value of business done.

The headline deal came on opening day, Nov. 6, when Weta FX, the New Zealand visual effects company behind “The Lord of the Rings” and “Avatar,” signed a memorandum of understanding with TAICCA aimed at making Taiwan an AI hub for Asia’s content industries. Weta FX will partner with Taiwanese animation and VFX outfit Moonshine Studio and will set up a technology platform to back Taiwanese film and TV projects, along with exchanges and internships for young Taiwanese filmmakers.

articles.title: ‘NAZA’ From ‘No Other Land’ Co-Directors Passes 1.5 Million Cinema Admissions Worldwide
articles.summary: “NAZA,” the hot-button documentary about killings in Gaza that won a special jury prize at the recent Venice Film Festival, had tallied more than 1.5 million theatrical admissions across 47 territories as of Nov. 6. That ranks it among the year’s most-watched documentaries on the big screen.
body: Italy is the standout. I Wonder opened the doc there on Sept. 29, soon after it debuted in Venice, and it has since drawn 717,517 admissions, nearly half the worldwide total. It is still on 379 screens. “NAZA” has topped the Italian box office and now sits third among documentaries in the country’s cinema history, trailing only “Fahrenheit 9/11” and “March of the Penguins.”

In the U.S., “NAZA” opened on Sept. 30, self-distributed via Michael Tuckman’s company mTuckman Media. Neon came on board as U.S. distributor in late October, with plans to take the film wider off the back of that first run. Admissions across the U.S. and Canada stand at 83,673.

Dogwoof opened the film in the U.K. and Ireland on Oct. 15 with an event screening at the Ritz. Abraham and Szor took part in a Q&A alongside producer Jim Wilson and executive producer Jonathan Glazer, and it was beamed live to 104 more cinemas. That night alone sold more than 7,000 tickets. The film went on to play the full Picturehouse circuit, sites from the Odeon, Cineworld and Vue chains, and a handful of independents. Its U.K. and Ireland total now stands at 102,509 admissions.

articles.title: Netflix’s Genre-Bending YA Drama ‘The Body’ Is a Queer Y2K Extravaganza: TV Review
articles.summary: Girlhood is a divine experience, a period when young women begin to discover who they are and who they might become. From “Under the Bridge” creator Quinn Shephard, Netflix’s teen drama “The Body” is a twisted coming-of-age narrative that pays homage to the 2000s, specifically films like “Bring It…
body: The eight-episode series opens on Halloween 2004. At St. Barth’s Catholic School, co-captains and best friends Anya Butler ( Kristina Bogic ) and Elise Zakaria ( Sara Boustany ), who call each other “wife,” hold emergency tryouts for the school’s all-girls dance troupe the Lions. Star dancer Maddie Delaney (Shirley Chen) has broken her ankle, and with the regional competition two weeks away, the team needs to fill her spot. Among the auditioners are Lisbeth Anderson (Geena Meszaros), who is new in town, and Grace Franklin (Sofia Wylie), the niece of Father Sam Franklin (Nnamdi Asomugha), the head of the school. Grace’s talent clearly surpasses Lisbeth’s.

Though Lisbeth’s dreams of becoming a Lion are dashed, her spirits lift when Anya, in an attempt at being polite, invites her to a Halloween party at the Devil’s House. In this abandoned convent, the Lions also plan to initiate Grace into the group. Eager to evade her hyper-religious, unwell mother, Catherine (Louisa Krause), Lisbeth urges her brother, Leo (Jackson Kelly), who has his own peculiarities and an obsessive crush on Grace, to cover for her so she can attend the party.
points: Girlhood is a divine experience, a period when young women begin to discover who they are and who they might become.

articles.title: Dua Lipa to become first female British headliner at Coachella 2027
articles.summary: The Training Season singer, Tame Impala and SZA will headline two weekends in the California desert.
body: Coachella has announced the line-up for its 2027 festival, with Dua Lipa set to be the first solo female British artist to headline.
The Training Season singer is top of Friday's bill for both weekends in April, with psych-rock band Tame Impala headlining the Saturday shows and US singer SZA closing out both Sundays.
The massive festival returns to the California desert on 9 to 11 and 16 to 18 April next year, with more than 100,000 fans expected to attend each day.
Madonna is also set to return to the festival after a surprise appearance alongside this year's headliner Sabrina Carpenter, 20 years on from her first Coachella set.

articles.title: Police told Russell Brand to leave Jemima Goldsmith's house in 2014
articles.summary: Police confirm they asked Brand to leave his ex-girlfriend's house after she reported an alleged assault.
body: Police have confirmed they told Russell Brand to leave his ex-girlfriend Jemima Goldsmith's house in 2014 after she claimed a violent incident took place.
Thames Valley Police said officers were contacted by an alleged victim and went to an address in Oxfordshire on 25 July 2014 but no arrests were made.
They listened to her concerns and gave support, and "also ensured the victim's partner left the address, as per the victim's wishes", the police added in a statement on Wednesday.
Goldsmith, who dated Brand for about a year, wrote on X on Monday that she "had to call the police to have him removed from my house in 2014 during a violent incident" but chose not to press charges.
points: Police confirm they asked Brand to leave his ex-girlfriend's house after she reported an alleged assault.

articles.title: ‘Apart’ Star Luca Pasqualino and Creator Stelana Kliris Unpack a Love Story Amid War and Apartheid
articles.summary: The film, starring Leem Lubany and inspired by the experiences of the writer-director's parents who emigrated from Cyprus to South Africa, opens Tallinn's Critics' Picks program.
body: Apart will get its world premiere at the 30th edition of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival ( PÖFF ) in Estonia on Friday, Nov. 13, opening its Critics’ Picks section.

“In 1974, when Turkey invades Cyprus, young Eleni (Lubany) leaves her homeland through an arranged marriage and finds herself in Apartheid South Africa, swapping one divided country for another,” teases a synopsis for the film. “There, a new life with Nico (Pasqualino) slowly turns into love, until an unexpected friendship forces her to confront a secret from her past.”

Kliris wrote and directed Apart and produced it with Susan Simnett, Jamie Harvey and Ioanna Bolomyti. The cinematographer is Simon Sarketzis, with Emilios Avraam handling editing. Reinvent Yellow Sales is handling sales. Watch a trailer for Apart right here.

Pasqualino, who is now back on Disney+ in the second part of season 2 of the hit show Rivals, and Kliris talked to THR about Apart, how it was shot in Cyprus and captures a 1970s aesthetic, casting challenges, and how urgent the themes explored in the film feel.

articles.title: Wayne Rooney leads I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here! line-up
articles.summary: The football star will be joined by Gavin and Stacey star Joanna Page and YouTuber Sharky among others.
body: Former England and Manchester United footballer Wayne Rooney, Gavin and Stacey star Joanna Page and YouTuber Sharky will be among the intrepid crew entering the jungle Down Under for this year's I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out Of Here!
They will be joined by Kaiser Chiefs frontman Ricky Wilson, Paralympian and presenter Ade Adepitan, actress Claire Sweeney and broadcaster Mariella Frostrup.
TV presenter AJ Odudu, comedian Jack Skipper, Love Island contestant Chloe Burrows and model Leomie Anderson round out the team headed for Australia.
Hosts Ant and Dec will return with the ITV show's opening episode on Monday, 16 November, with the series now in its 26th year.
